page.metaDescription: Browse every operation of the forum's REST API, see what it takes and what it answers, and try it from the page.
page.title: API reference

intro.lead: Everything this site does goes through one REST API, and you can call it from your own tools. The reference below is built from the live specification and lets you try each operation.
intro.authSession: While you are signed in, Try it out runs as you, with your session. Signed out, it runs as a guest. If every call answers 401 and you sent no key, your session has ended: sign out and in again.
intro.authKey: To call the API from your own scripts and tools, use an API key and send it as a Bearer token: Authorization: Bearer your-key. In the reference, press Authorize and paste the key to try operations with it. The page keeps the key in memory only and forgets it when you leave or reload.
intro.createKey: Create a key while you are signed in, with POST /api/auth/api-key/create (under Api-key, "Create a new API key for a user"). Its body also needs your current password in password. The key is shown once, so copy it then, and treat it like a password: it acts as you.
intro.keysAccess: A key can do what its owner can do, with these exceptions.
intro.keysManage: Through the sign-in service (/api/auth) it cannot create, list or revoke keys, change the password, email address or username, or open a session.
intro.keysPassword: It is refused on every operation that asks for your password, such as changing groups, permissions, moderators and promotions, or erasing a member. Those need a signed-in session. So do accepting the terms and rules, and reading your sessions and sign-in history.
intro.keysEnd: A key stops working when its owner is banned or erased, when it expires, and when the owner's password is changed or reset or the owner is signed out everywhere.
intro.limitsRate: Requests are limited per minute, and reads, writes and searches are counted apart. Past a limit the API answers 429 with a Retry-After header.
intro.limitsStaff: Operations that only staff may use are listed too. If you are not signed in the API answers 401, if you lack the permission it answers 403, and if the thing is hidden from you it answers 404.
